lines.intro: Not a normal volcano. A supervolcano, hiding under a national park. Here's what would actually happen, step by step.
lines.relate: You know when you shake a soda and open it too fast? Now imagine that, but the soda is a giant pool of melted rock under Wyoming.
lines.signs: Week one. Small earthquakes hit every day, and the ground starts to swell. Scientists watching it around the clock sound the alarm.
lines.blast: Then it blows. A column of ash shoots more than twenty kilometers into the sky. Everyone near the park gets evacuated.
lines.ash: Week two. Ash rains down across America. Near the park, it's deep enough to crush roofs. Far away, just a few centimeters still shuts down roads, planes and farms.
lines.summer: Then the weather changes. Ash and gas block some sunlight, and summers get colder for years. Crops struggle all over the world.
lines.twist: But here's the crazy part. Yellowstone isn't overdue. Scientists say the chance of a super eruption in any given year is about one in seven hundred thirty thousand.
lines.real: So could this really happen? The last one was about six hundred thirty thousand years ago. And when a different volcano erupted in Indonesia in 1815, the next year was called the year without a summer.
lines.end: The far more likely event? A small steam blast or a lava flow inside the park. Scary for tourists, but nothing like the movies.
lines.cta: So be honest... would you still visit Yellowstone? Tell me in the comments.
